app_description: A CLI tool for file analysis
opt_size: Show file sizes with specified unit (auto, b/bytes, kb/kilobytes, mb/megabytes, gb/gigabytes, tb/terabytes)
opt_properties: Show detailed file properties and analysis
opt_disk: Disk operations: 'list' to show all disks, or specify disk name for info
opt_search: Search for files using regex pattern
opt_extension: Only list files with the specified extension (e.g. rs, txt, pdf)
opt_sort_by: Sort files by: name, size, date
opt_content_dups: Verify duplicates by content hash (slower, true duplicates only)
opt_hash: Hash algorithm for content-based duplicate detection (sha256 or md5)
opt_directory: Analyze a directory as a whole (not its contents)
opt_json: Output results as JSON to stdout
opt_whole: Analyze the path as a whole (auto-detects if file or directory)
opt_lines: Count lines in files (uses path argument or current directory)
opt_preview: Preview file contents (N, f/N, or l/N for first/last N lines)
opt_larger_than: Filter files larger than threshold (e.g. 10MB, 1GB, 8 GB, 2MiB, 1GiB, or path to file)
opt_smaller_than: Filter files smaller than threshold (e.g. 1KB, 500MB, 500 MB, 2MiB, 1GiB, or path to file)
opt_equal_to: Filter files equal to threshold (e.g. 10MB, 1GB, 8 GB, 2MiB, 1GiB, or path to file)
opt_older_than: Filter files older than duration (e.g. 30d, 2w, 1y, yyyy-mm-dd)
opt_newer_than: Filter files newer than duration (e.g. 7d, 1w, 7 d)
opt_empty: Show only empty files and directories
opt_delete_duplicates: Delete duplicate files, keeping the first occurrence
opt_merge_duplicates: Merge duplicate files by hard linking (keeps first, links rest)
opt_content: Search for pattern inside file contents
opt_top: Show the N largest files in a directory
opt_stat: Show a summary of directory statistics (file count, total size, etc.)
opt_force: Skip confirmation prompts for destructive actions
opt_language_value: Set language directly (e.g. english, chinese_simplified, japanese)
warning_large_dir: Warning: Depending on the directory size it can take quite a bit of time to analyze. Use arguments for a more specific and fast result.
